headline: Two oil tankers set ablaze by naval mines on 'illegal route' south of Hormuz
dek: IRGC: last night its air defense struck and destroyed a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz (54th claimed); IRGC Navy mines exploded at the 'illegal route' south of Hormuz, setting two 'violating' oil tankers ablaze and halting them. Statement warns: 'If these mischiefs by the arrogant US…
sources: IRGC public relations, Statement No. 19, via official Sepah News website
fault_line: Who controls Hormuz and who pays at the pump — Iran's sovereignty/enforcement vs US escorts and the sanctions blockade; is Tehran's 'authorization' regime piracy, or the only leverage a blockaded country has?

sections.what_happened: IRGC: last night its air defense struck and destroyed a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz (54th claimed); IRGC Navy mines exploded at the 'illegal route' south of Hormuz, setting two 'violating' oil tankers ablaze and halting them. Statement warns: 'If these mischiefs by the arrogant US regime continue, oil companies will have to pay a greater price.'
sections.what_verified: AFP carried the statement verbatim via Dawn live updates; ISNA published full statement text; Mehr/Fars/Roya News (Roya: ~2M barrels crude each, no tanker names or casualty details given); Al Jazeera liveblog (10:00 GMT 'just joining': 'IRGC says two tankers have caught fire after hitting mines'); Al Mayadeen/Roya/see.news. No independent/US-side confirmation of the incident itself in-window.
sections.what_disputed: No tanker names, flags, owners, casualties, or images released by any source; US/UKMTO has not confirmed; Iran has a documented pattern of inflating Hormuz incident claims; RVCJ Media viral graphic claiming 'IRAN DECLARES STRAIT OF HORMUZ CLOSED' has NO reliable-source backing — Iran's stated position is an authorization requirement, not a declared closure.
sections.why_matters: Two oil tankers burning in Hormuz while Brent holds $110 — the world is paying for a choke point nobody controls. Iran says 'violating tankers will burn'; Washington says 'not one Iranian barrel gets through.' Both claims, both receipts, neither with full proof — that's the real story: an undeclared tanker war running on statements, mines, and insurance premiums.
sections.context: Background: IRGC Statement No. 19: two oil tankers set ablaze by naval mines on 'illegal route' south of Hormuz; US MQ-9 downed overnight

Iran says 'violating tankers will burn'; Washington says 'not one Iranian barrel gets through.' Both claims, both receipts, neither with full proof — that's the real story: an undeclared tanker war running on statements, mines, and insurance premiums.
